outputs.L1: Described herein are computer-based methods and apparatuses, including computer program products, for the centralized deployment of advertising code. outputs.L2: Computer-implemented techniques and systems are disclosed, including computer program products, for deploying advertising code from a centralized location. The advertising code is maintained for use by a web page and includes one or more of vendor advertising code and vendor reporting code. An application programming interface is made available so the web page can retrieve the advertising code. Through this interface, the advertising code may be revised so that the web page automatically receives the updated version without requiring modifications to the source code used by the web page to access the advertising code. outputs.L3:
Computer-based methods and apparatuses are provided for the centralized deployment and management of advertising code. In these systems, advertising code used by a web page is stored in a centralized location rather than being embedded directly and permanently in the source code of the web page. The stored advertising code may include, for example, vendor advertising code, vendor reporting code, tracking code, analytics code, or other code associated with the delivery, measurement, or reporting of online advertisements.

A web page is configured to access the stored advertising code through an application programming interface. By using the application programming interface, the web page can request and receive advertising code as needed, without requiring changes to the web page’s underlying source code whenever the advertising code is modified. This allows updates to vendor code, reporting logic, advertising tags, or related scripts to be made centrally and then delivered automatically to web pages that use the interface.

In operation, a request for advertising code is received from the web page through the application programming interface. In response to the request, the system identifies the appropriate advertising code for that web page or advertising context. The system then selects the most recently updated version of the advertising code available for use. Once selected, the updated advertising code is transmitted to the requesting web page through the application programming interface.

As a result, advertising code can be deployed, revised, and maintained in a centralized manner. Web pages can receive current versions of advertising or reporting code without requiring manual updates to each individual page’s source code, thereby improving efficiency, consistency, and manageability in online advertising operations.
outputs.L4:
Computer-based methods and apparatuses are provided for centrally deploying and maintaining advertising code used by web pages, applications, or other network-accessible content. In one implementation, advertising code, reporting code, tracking code, or other vendor-supplied executable or embeddable code is stored in a centralized repository accessible through a server system. The stored code may be associated with one or more vendors, advertising campaigns, publishers, web properties, page locations, account identifiers, or configuration parameters.

A web page that is intended to display an advertisement or perform advertising-related reporting includes a call to an application programming interface rather than containing the full vendor advertising code directly in the page source. When the web page is requested or rendered, the page invokes the application programming interface and provides information identifying the page, publisher, advertising placement, campaign, vendor, or other relevant context. In response, the server system retrieves the appropriate advertising or reporting code from the centralized repository and returns it to the requesting web page.

The server system is configured to provide the most recently updated version of the applicable advertising code. Accordingly, when a vendor modifies its advertising script, tracking pixel, reporting tag, or other code, the updated code can be stored centrally without requiring manual modification of each web page that uses the code. Subsequent requests made through the application programming interface automatically receive the updated version. This allows advertising code to be changed, corrected, replaced, or reconfigured across multiple web pages or sites from a central location.

The system may include one or more databases for storing advertising code and associated metadata, one or more web servers or application servers for receiving requests from web pages, and one or more interfaces for adding, editing, approving, versioning, or publishing code updates. The centralized repository may maintain current and prior versions of advertising code, allowing administrators to audit changes, restore earlier versions, or control when a new version becomes active. Access controls may be used to restrict which users or vendors may upload or modify code.

In operation, a publisher may place a lightweight reference, script call, tag, or other application programming interface invocation in the source code of a web page. The reference remains substantially unchanged even when the underlying advertising vendor code changes. When a user accesses the web page, the browser or page execution environment sends a request to the centralized system. The centralized system determines which advertising code should be served, obtains the latest active version of that code, and returns the code to the browser for execution or inclusion in the page.

By separating the web page source code from the underlying advertising and reporting code, the described methods and apparatuses simplify deployment and maintenance of advertising integrations. The approach reduces the need for repeated source-code edits, lowers the risk of outdated advertising tags remaining on pages, and enables faster propagation of vendor updates. It also provides a centralized point for managing, validating, and monitoring advertising code across multiple pages, sites, campaigns, or publishers. As a result, advertising code can be updated automatically and consistently without requiring individual changes to each web page that uses the advertising functionality.
outputs.L5:
**The Role of Advertising**

Advertising can be described as a powerful tool used to communicate messages about products, services, ideas, or brands. The main purpose of advertising is to attract attention, create interest, and encourage people to take action, such as buying a product or learning more about a company.

The world of advertising has changed greatly over time. In the past, advertisements were mostly found in newspapers, magazines, radio, and television. Today, digital advertising plays a major role, appearing on websites, social media platforms, search engines, and mobile apps. This allows businesses to reach specific audiences more easily and measure the success of their campaigns.

Effective advertising is not only about selling something. It is also about building trust, creating emotional connections, and making a brand memorable. A well-described advertisement clearly explains the benefits of a product or service while also appealing to the needs and interests of the audience.

In conclusion, advertising is an important part of modern communication. The way a message is described and presented can strongly influence how people think, feel, and act.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an invention about centrally hosting and updating third-party advertising code for websites through an API.
counterfactuals.output: A system and method are disclosed for centrally hosting, managing, and updating third-party advertising code for deployment on publisher websites through an application programming interface (API). The system stores advertising scripts, tags, configuration data, and related execution rules in a central repository and exposes API endpoints through which participating websites retrieve or invoke the applicable advertising code at runtime or during page generation. Updates to third-party advertising code, including script revisions, vendor changes, targeting parameters, consent controls, and performance optimizations, are performed at the central repository and propagated to one or more websites without requiring manual modification of website source code. The system may authenticate API requests, select advertising code based on publisher identity, page context, user consent status, geography, device type, or other criteria, and return executable code, references to hosted code, or configuration instructions. Centralized monitoring, version control, rollback, and logging may be provided to improve security, compliance, and operational reliability. The invention thereby enables website operators to integrate and maintain third-party advertising functionality through a controlled API-based infrastructure while reducing implementation burden and facilitating rapid updates across multiple websites.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a legalistic summary of computer-based methods and apparatuses for deploying vendor ad code and reporting code to web pages without requiring source code changes.
counterfactuals.output:
Disclosed are computer-based methods, systems, and apparatuses for deploying vendor advertising code, analytics code, tracking code, reporting code, or other third-party executable or declarative code to one or more web pages without requiring modification of the underlying source code of such web pages.

In one implementation, a deployment platform comprises at least one processor, memory, and one or more network interfaces configured to receive, store, manage, and selectively deliver code snippets or tag configurations associated with one or more vendors. A website operator may define, through an administrative interface, rules specifying when, where, and under what conditions particular vendor code is to be injected, rendered, executed, or otherwise made available in connection with a web page. Such rules may be based on page URL, page type, user segment, device type, browser characteristic, geographic location, consent state, campaign identifier, timing condition, or other contextual parameter.

The system may operate by causing a previously installed container script, proxy component, edge-injection component, browser-executed loader, content management integration, server-side middleware, or similar deployment mechanism to retrieve configuration data from the deployment platform. Based on the retrieved configuration data, the mechanism dynamically inserts, references, executes, or transmits vendor ad code and reporting code in association with the requested web page. In this manner, additions, deletions, updates, or substitutions of vendor code may be performed centrally through the deployment platform, without editing, rebuilding, redeploying, or otherwise modifying the original web page source code.

In certain embodiments, the apparatus further includes a rule engine configured to evaluate deployment conditions, a code repository configured to store vendor scripts or script references, a versioning component configured to maintain historical configurations, an approval workflow configured to regulate publication of code changes, and a monitoring component configured to detect execution status, errors, latency, or compliance events. The reporting code may collect impression data, click data, conversion data, viewability data, user interaction data, diagnostic data, or other telemetry, and may transmit such data to one or more reporting endpoints, including vendor systems, publisher systems, or centralized analytics services.

The system may further provide safeguards including sandboxing, asynchronous loading, consent enforcement, content security policy compatibility, vendor permission management, audit logging, rollback functionality, and validation of code prior to deployment. In some embodiments, the platform supports both client-side deployment, in which code is delivered to and executed by a browser, and server-side or edge-side deployment, in which code, beacons, parameters, or reporting events are assembled, modified, or transmitted before or during delivery of the web page to the client device.

Accordingly, the disclosed methods and apparatuses enable centralized, configurable, and repeatable deployment of advertising and reporting functionality across web properties while minimizing or eliminating the need for direct source code changes to individual pages. The techniques may reduce engineering effort, accelerate vendor onboarding, improve governance of third-party code, and provide controlled distribution and reporting of advertising-related functionality.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in patent application language, a computer program product for centralized deployment of advertising scripts to web pages using an application programming interface.
counterfactuals.output:
A computer program product is provided for centralized deployment of advertising scripts to web pages using an application programming interface (API). The computer program product comprises a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having computer-executable instructions stored thereon which, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform operations for receiving, storing, configuring, and distributing advertising script code to a plurality of publisher web pages.

In one embodiment, the computer program product includes instructions for providing a centralized script management service accessible via an API. The API is configured to receive, from an authorized client device or advertising management system, one or more advertising script definitions. Each advertising script definition may include script code, a script identifier, placement information, targeting parameters, version information, activation criteria, priority data, scheduling data, or combinations thereof. The centralized script management service stores the advertising script definitions in association with one or more web page identifiers, publisher account identifiers, domain identifiers, placement identifiers, or ad inventory identifiers.

The computer program product further includes instructions for generating, for each of a plurality of web pages, a deployment instruction or loader reference configured to be embedded in the web page. The loader reference may comprise a tag, script element, software development kit call, or other executable reference that, when executed by a client browser or web application, communicates with the centralized script management service or a content delivery endpoint. In response to receiving a request associated with the loader reference, the centralized script management service determines one or more advertising scripts to be deployed to the requesting web page based at least in part on information contained in the request, stored configuration data, and applicable deployment rules.

In certain embodiments, the API comprises one or more endpoints configured to allow creation, retrieval, updating, deletion, activation, deactivation, testing, rollback, or versioning of advertising scripts. The API may further be configured to receive commands that associate advertising scripts with particular pages, page groups, domains, placements, geographic regions, user segments, device types, browser types, time periods, advertising campaigns, or other contextual conditions. The API may also expose status information, deployment history, error information, audit records, and performance metrics associated with deployed advertising scripts.

Upon determining an advertising script to be deployed, the computer program product causes the one or more processors to provide the script, or a reference to the script, to the requesting web page. The provided script may be dynamically assembled, selected from a cached version, retrieved from a storage repository, or delivered through a content delivery network. In one embodiment, the delivered script includes instructions for rendering an advertisement, requesting an advertisement from an ad server, loading a third-party advertising library, tracking an impression, measuring viewability, recording user interaction, or performing bidding-related operations.

The computer program product may further include instructions for validating advertising script definitions prior to deployment. Validation may include determining whether script syntax, source domains, security attributes, sandboxing requirements, content security policy requirements, permission settings, size limits, or execution constraints satisfy one or more predetermined rules. If a received advertising script definition fails validation, the centralized script management service may reject the definition, prevent activation of the script, provide an error response via the API, or store the script in an inactive state.

In another embodiment, the computer program product provides version control for advertising scripts. A first version of an advertising script may be deployed to a first set of web pages while a second version is deployed to a second set of web pages. The centralized script management service may maintain prior versions and may permit rollback to an earlier version in response to an API request, detected error condition, performance threshold, or administrator command.

The computer program product may also include instructions for selectively deploying advertising scripts according to a rules engine. The rules engine may evaluate one or more deployment rules comprising targeting rules, frequency rules, consent rules, privacy rules, page-context rules, device rules, campaign rules, or publisher-specific rules. Based on the evaluation, the system may determine whether to deploy a script, which script version to deploy, where in the web page to execute the script, and whether the script should be loaded synchronously, asynchronously, lazily, or after occurrence of a browser event.

In some embodiments, the API is secured using authentication and authorization mechanisms, including API keys, tokens, signed requests, OAuth credentials, role-based access controls, or publisher-specific permissions. The centralized script management service may determine whether a requesting entity is authorized to create, modify, or deploy an advertising script for a particular publisher, domain, web page, or placement.

The computer program product may further include instructions for monitoring deployed advertising scripts. Monitoring may include collecting execution data, error reports, latency information, impression counts, fill-rate data, click data, revenue data, viewability data, consent status, and browser compatibility information. The collected data may be associated with script identifiers, version identifiers, page identifiers, placement identifiers, or publisher identifiers, and may be made available through one or more reporting API endpoints.

In one illustrative implementation, a publisher includes a single persistent loader script on each of a plurality of web pages. Rather than manually editing each web page to add, remove, or modify advertising script code, an administrator transmits configuration instructions to the centralized script management service through the API. The service stores the configuration instructions and, when the persistent loader script is executed by a user browser accessing one of the web pages, the service returns advertising script code selected in accordance with the stored configuration instructions. In this manner, advertising scripts may be centrally updated and deployed across multiple web pages without requiring direct modification of the source code of each web page.

In claim-style language, the computer program product may be characterized as follows:

A computer program product comprising a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to: provide an application programming interface configured to receive an advertising script configuration from an authorized remote computing device; store, in a centralized repository, an advertising script associated with the advertising script configuration; associate the advertising script with at least one web page identifier corresponding to at least one web page; receive, from a client device executing a loader script embedded in the at least one web page, a request for advertising script content; determine, based at least in part on the advertising script configuration and the request, that the advertising script is to be deployed to the at least one web page; and transmit, to the client device, the advertising script or a reference thereto for execution in connection with presentation of the at least one web page.

In additional embodiments, the stored instructions further cause the one or more processors to validate the advertising script before activation, maintain multiple versions of the advertising script, select among the multiple versions based on deployment rules, expose API endpoints for modifying deployment criteria, and collect execution metrics associated with the advertising script after deployment.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for a technology that stores advertising code on a computing device and serves updated versions to webpages through API requests.
counterfactuals.output: A technology is provided for locally storing and serving advertising code to webpages. A computing device receives advertising code from a remote system and stores the code in local memory, such as a browser cache, application storage, or other persistent storage. When a webpage requires an advertisement or advertising function, the webpage issues an application programming interface (API) request to the computing device. In response, the computing device retrieves the stored advertising code and provides it to the webpage for execution or rendering. The computing device may determine whether the stored advertising code is current by checking version information, expiration data, update policies, or communication with a remote server. If an updated version is available, the computing device obtains the updated advertising code, stores it locally, and serves the updated version in response to subsequent API requests. This approach reduces network latency, limits repeated downloads, improves advertisement delivery reliability, and enables consistent updating of advertising functionality across webpages.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
